# pki — X.509 certificates, OCSP and CRLs

[All groups](README.md)

## pki decode

Decode X.509 certificates, chains, CSRs and CRLs (PEM or base64 DER): subject, SANs, key, every common extension, fingerprints. Checks validity, key size, signature algorithm, SAN presence, CA flags, chain order, CSR self-signature and CRL freshness and signature.

MCP tool: `pki_decode`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--input` | string | PEM (any number of blocks) or base64 DER; a path from the CLI or a profile; - for stdin. **Required.** CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--hostname` | string | Check that the first certificate is valid for this host name or IP. |
| `--issuer-cert` | string | Issuer certificate, to verify a CRL's signature. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--check-serial` | string | Serial number (hex) to look up in the CRL. |

Plus the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## pki verify

Verify a certificate chain (leaf first, then intermediates) against the system trust store or supplied roots, for a host name and key usage, now or at a given time. Returns every valid path.

MCP tool: `pki_verify`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--chain` | string | PEM chain, leaf first. **Required.** CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--roots` | string | PEM root certificates to trust instead of the system store. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--hostname` | string | Host name or IP the leaf must be valid for. |
| `--usage` | string | Required extended key usage. Default `server`. One of `server`, `client`, `any`. |
| `--at-time` | string | Verify as of this RFC 3339 time. |

Plus the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## pki ca

Create a throwaway test PKI: a root CA, optionally an intermediate and an issuing CA, and an end-entity certificate (server, client or both) with chosen SANs and extensions. Returns PEM certificates and private keys; with out_dir (CLI only) also writes them to files. For testing only.

MCP tool: `pki_ca`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--levels` | int | CA levels: 1 (root signs leaves), 2 (root and issuing CA) or 3 (root, intermediate, issuing). Default `3`. |
| `--root-cn` | string | Root CA common name. Default `idpdbg Test Root CA`. |
| `--ca-key-type` | string | Key algorithm for the CAs. Default `ecdsa-p384`. One of `ecdsa-p256`, `ecdsa-p384`, `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `rsa-4096`, `ed25519`. |
| `--permitted-dns` | list | Name constraint: DNS domains the issuing CA may issue for. |
| `--out-dir` | string | CLI only: write the PEM files here (existing files are never overwritten). |
| `--cn` | string | Subject common name. Default `localhost`. |
| `--organization` | string | Subject organization. |
| `--dns-names` | list | DNS subjectAltNames. Default `localhost`. |
| `--ip-addresses` | list | IP subjectAltNames. Default `127.0.0.1,::1`. |
| `--emails` | list | Email subjectAltNames. |
| `--uris` | list | URI subjectAltNames, e.g. spiffe://example.org/workload. |
| `--usage` | string | Extended key usage. Default `server`. One of `server`, `client`, `both`, `email`, `code`. |
| `--validity-days` | int | Lifetime in days. Default `90`. |
| `--key-type` | string | Key algorithm. Default `ecdsa-p256`. One of `ecdsa-p256`, `ecdsa-p384`, `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `rsa-4096`, `ed25519`. |
| `--crl-urls` | list | CRL distribution point URLs. |
| `--ocsp-urls` | list | OCSP responder URLs (authorityInfoAccess). |
| `--ca-issuers-urls` | list | caIssuers URLs (authorityInfoAccess). |
| `--policies` | list | Certificate policy OIDs, e.g. 2.23.140.1.2.1. |
| `--must-staple` | bool | Add the TLS Feature (OCSP must-staple) extension. |

Plus the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## pki issue

Issue an end-entity certificate from an existing CA certificate and key, with chosen SANs, key usage and extensions (CRL, OCSP, caIssuers, policies, must-staple). Returns the certificate, a new private key and the chain.

MCP tool: `pki_issue`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--issuer-cert` | string | Issuing CA certificate (PEM; may include its own chain after it). **Required.** May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--issuer-key` | string | Issuing CA private key (PEM). **Required.** May be a file path (CLI or profile only). Over MCP it must be passed in the call, never taken from a profile or the environment. |
| `--out-dir` | string | CLI only: write the PEM files here (existing files are never overwritten). |
| `--cn` | string | Subject common name. Default `localhost`. |
| `--organization` | string | Subject organization. |
| `--dns-names` | list | DNS subjectAltNames. Default `localhost`. |
| `--ip-addresses` | list | IP subjectAltNames. Default `127.0.0.1,::1`. |
| `--emails` | list | Email subjectAltNames. |
| `--uris` | list | URI subjectAltNames, e.g. spiffe://example.org/workload. |
| `--usage` | string | Extended key usage. Default `server`. One of `server`, `client`, `both`, `email`, `code`. |
| `--validity-days` | int | Lifetime in days. Default `90`. |
| `--key-type` | string | Key algorithm. Default `ecdsa-p256`. One of `ecdsa-p256`, `ecdsa-p384`, `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `rsa-4096`, `ed25519`. |
| `--crl-urls` | list | CRL distribution point URLs. |
| `--ocsp-urls` | list | OCSP responder URLs (authorityInfoAccess). |
| `--ca-issuers-urls` | list | caIssuers URLs (authorityInfoAccess). |
| `--policies` | list | Certificate policy OIDs, e.g. 2.23.140.1.2.1. |
| `--must-staple` | bool | Add the TLS Feature (OCSP must-staple) extension. |

Plus the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## pki ocsp

Check a certificate's revocation status over OCSP (RFC 6960): finds the issuer (from the chain, issuer, or the caIssuers URL), asks the responder named in the certificate (or url), and checks the response signature, a delegated responder's authorization, the certificate status with revocation time and reason, and freshness (thisUpdate/nextUpdate). Can instead check a captured response, such as a TLS server's stapled one.

MCP tool: `pki_ocsp`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--cert` | string | Certificate (PEM or base64 DER); a PEM chain may follow it. **Required.** CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--issuer` | string | Issuer certificate, if not in the chain or fetchable. CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--url` | string | Responder URL instead of the certificate's own. |
| `--response` | string | A captured OCSP response (base64 DER) to check instead of querying. CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. |
| `--hash` | string | Hash for the request's CertID. Default `sha1`. One of `sha1`, `sha256`. |

Plus the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## pki crl

Check a certificate's revocation status against its CRL (RFC 5280): finds the issuer, downloads the CRL from the certificate's distribution points over http(s) or from a directory over ldap(s) (Active Directory Certificate Services' ldap:/// locations included), or takes a supplied one, and checks the CRL's issuer and signature, freshness, scope (issuingDistributionPoint shards: only CA or end-entity certificates, some reasons, the URL it was fetched from), then whether the serial is listed, with time and reason. Where the CA publishes delta CRLs (freshestCRL), fetches the delta, checks that it belongs to the base CRL, and merges it: newer revocations, and certificates released from hold. For CAs that publish no OCSP (Let's Encrypt, Google Trust Services).

MCP tool: `pki_crl`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--cert` | string | Certificate (PEM or base64 DER); a PEM chain may follow it. **Required.** CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--issuer` | string | Issuer certificate, if not in the chain or fetchable. CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--crl` | string | A CRL (PEM or base64 DER) to check instead of downloading. CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--delta-crl` | string | A delta CRL (PEM or base64 DER) to apply instead of downloading the one the CRL or certificate names (freshestCRL). CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--ldap-url` | string | Directory for ldap:/// CRL locations that name no host, as Active Directory Certificate Services writes them, e.g. ldaps://dc1.corp.example; default: the domain in the entry's DN. |
| `--starttls` | bool | Upgrade ldap:// connections for CRLs with StartTLS. |
| `--bind-dn` | string | DN to bind as to read CRLs from the directory in ldap_url (needs ldaps:// or starttls); other directories, which the certificate chose, are read anonymously. |
| `--ldap-password` | string | Bind password (prefer env IDPDBG_LDAP_PASSWORD or a profile). Secret: falls back to `IDPDBG_LDAP_PASSWORD`, redacted in traces. |

Plus the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).
